source.title: Intriguing Properties of Large Language and Vision Models
source.authors: Young-Jun Lee; ByungSoo Ko; Han-Gyu Kim; Yechan Hwang; Ho-Jin Choi

record.file_problem: None; the paper text is present through its appendices.
record.tranche_reason: It measures cross-modal representation alignment before and after visual instruction tuning and reports that alignment degrades, qualifying claims of preserved or general convergence. It does not test a scale-driven increase in alignment.
record.gate_note: The alignment result is reported for DOCCI using mutual nearest-neighbor alignment, with a comparison to the original vision encoder. Other performance results in the paper, including classification and permutation tests, do not measure the claim versions. Figure 7 also plots results across LLM families, but the pasted figure text does not preserve extractable values for each plotted point.
record.test_reason: Section 3.6 applies the Platonic Representation Hypothesis's mutual nearest-neighbour metric on DOCCI image-caption pairs. It measures how alignment between 10 LLMs and the vision representation changes from CLIP to the instruction-tuned LLaVA. This is a new setting (post-hoc visual instruction tuning) with a direct result on cross-modal alignment.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also frame the result as LLVMs losing the ability to understand 'shared world concepts' under the Platonic hypothesis. They link the alignment drop to catastrophic forgetting from overemphasising complex-reasoning tasks, and they question the projector's role.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the mutual nearest-neighbor alignment metric discussed in the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, but applies it to alignment changes after visual instruction tuning rather than testing scale-driven convergence among independently trained models.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper evaluates alignment on DOCCI; it does not report a comparison across alternative metrics or input datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Zero-shot classification accuracy of LLaVA drops 22–29 points on average versus the CLIP encoders (Table 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Visual instruction tuning causes forgetting of the vision encoder's perceptual capability; this is a capability measure, not representational alignment.

record.problems: The alignment finding is given without numerical values or uncertainty in the text; Figure 7's per-model values are not extractable from the supplied figure text. The reported textual conclusion covers two LLVMs and does not isolate why alignment declines.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 7 plots alignment results across ten LLM configurations and two vision-encoder/LLaVA settings. Individual plotted points were not added as separate rows because the supplied text does not preserve their values or clearly assign them to each plotted model. Other reported results do not measure alignment or another claim version.

untested.parts: No comparison of independently trained models across scale; LLM size varies in Fig. 7, but no size trend is reported.
It does not test whether alignment rises as LLM size or quality increases, though Fig. 7 spans LLM sizes; it reports only the CLIP→LLaVA shift.
No mapping or stitching test; model-stitching is discussed only as background.
One metric and one dataset (DOCCI); no variation of metric, k, or inputs.
No test of plateauing or of shared data as the cause.

missing.what: Per-LLM mutual-kNN alignment values for CLIP vs LLaVA across 10 LLMs of differing sizes (BLOOM 0.56B–7B, OLMo, Gemma, Vicuna). These are needed to check any trend of alignment with LLM size, and whether the drop holds for every LLM.

record.verdict_notes: Mutual-kNN values are only plotted; the text gives no numbers, k, or uncertainty. The tuned model is counted as 'more capable' only on reasoning benchmarks, since its perception drops, so the V2 bearing is qualified.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test whether alignment between independently trained models rises with model size or capability.
It does not test whether image-caption alignment rises as both vision and language models improve.
No comparison of networks trained from different seeds or of their shared features or subspaces.
No test of mapping, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired interchangeability.
No test of recurring interpretable features or circuits.
The study does not compare similarity metrics, metric settings, or input distributions for the alignment result.

The result concerns alignment after visual instruction tuning; it does not establish that alignment plateaus or that shared training data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, explain alignment.

rows.subject: LLaVA-1.5
rows.operation_detail: Measured cross-modal representation alignment using mutual nearest-neighbor alignment; compared the tuned model with its original vision encoder.

conditions.value: visual instruction-tuned LLaVA-1.5 versus original vision encoder

rows.baseline: Representations of the original vision encoder (CLIP ViT-L/336px)
rows.value: Alignment after visual instruction tuning is reported as degraded relative to the original vision encoder; exact value not stated in text.
rows.note: The paper explicitly describes degraded alignment. Figure 7 plots results across LLM families, but individual plotted values are not extractable from the supplied text.
rows.check: The subject is the alignment of LLaVA-1.5's vision-side representations with 10 LLMs (BLOOM 0.56B–7B, OLMo 1B/7B, Gemma 2B/7B, Vicuna-1.5 7B), versus CLIP-L/336px. The decline is observed, and the axis range (~0.2–0.3) shows alignment far from complete. For V2 it is a counter-case: the model gains reasoning ability but loses alignment. Its perception (Table 3) also drops, so 'better' is ambiguous. The text gives no per-point values.

relationships.condition: Vision representations after visual instruction tuning (LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-NeXT) vs their CLIP encoders, aligned against 10 LLMs on DOCCI
relationships.reason: Further training that adds reasoning ability lowers image-caption alignment with LLMs, so capability gains need not raise alignment. Perception also fell (Table 3), making 'better' ambiguous (R1, R2).
relationships.display_finding: LLaVA-1.5 and LLaVA-NeXT vision representations aligned less with 10 language models than their CLIP encoders did; perception also declined despite added reasoning ability.

source_check.condition: Vision representations after visual instruction tuning (LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-NeXT) vs their CLIP encoders, aligned against 10 LLMs on DOCCI
source_check.reason: R1 and R2 establish degraded alignment after tuning, but not that both modality models became better. Perception also declines, and the reasoning analysis is a separate comparison. V2's capability–alignment relationship remains untested under this condition; untested antecedents do not warrant limits_scope.

relationships.reason: Alignment shifts with the training objective (instruction tuning) and stays low (~0.2–0.3 on the Fig. 7 axis). This fits the view that objectives shape alignment, which is far from complete (R1, R2).
relationships.display_finding: Mutual-kNN alignment stayed around 0.2–0.3 and shifted with instruction tuning, indicating sensitivity to the training objective.

tranche.reason: The study applies the existing alignment metric in a new setting: preservation of cross-modal alignment after visual instruction tuning.

source_check.notes: Figure 7's individual scores are not recoverable from the supplied text; its axis ticks are not per-model measurements. The paper concerns projected visual representations and does not isolate a causal training-objective explanation.

statements.correction: Section 3.6: lower DOCCI mutual-nearest-neighbor alignment for LLaVA-1.5 and LLaVA-NeXT than their original CLIP encoders; Table 3: lower image-classification accuracy; Figure 4: mathematical-reasoning performance associated with instruction-data scale across LLVMs, a separate comparison.
statements.problem: The alignment and perception declines are supported. A matched reasoning improvement over the original CLIP encoder is not established, so this is not a demonstrated exception to V2 under joint capability improvement.
